title: k-th smallest in a sorted matrix
statement: Each row and each column of an n × n matrix is sorted ascending. Return the k-th smallest element (counting duplicates).
hints: n sorted rows: merge them with a heap holding one frontier element per row.
Or binary search on the value, counting elements ≤ x with a staircase walk in O(n).
complexity: O(k log n) merge, or O(n log(range)) by value

solution.explanation: k-way merge: a heap holds the next unconsumed element of each row; pop k − 1 times, pushing the popped element's right neighbour. Alternatively binary search on the answer (Part 2): count(≤ x) is a monotone O(n) staircase walk from the bottom-left. The second wins when k is close to n².
solution.python:
import heapq

import heapq

def kth_smallest(matrix, k):
    n = len(matrix)
    h = [(matrix[i][0], i, 0) for i in range(n)]
    heapq.heapify(h)
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        v, i, j = heapq.heappop(h)
        if j + 1 < n:
            heapq.heappush(h, (matrix[i][j + 1], i, j + 1))
    return h[0][0]
